domain: Political Philosophy / Constitutional Theory / Legitimacy Studies
topic_summary: Analysis of the monarchy vs. republic legitimacy contest as a contested kernel over sovereign authority grounding. The kernel is the sovereign-legitimacy commitment itself — the claim that some entity holds legitimate authority to rule. Monarchical and republican readings interpret this kernel through fundamentally different authority sources: inherited divine/traditional right versus delegated popular consent. This is an authority-axis case where the readings emit structurally different constraints with different beneficiary/victim structures and different mechanisms for legitimacy validation.

key_entities: Monarchical systems (inherited sovereignty; divine right tradition)
Absolute monarchy (autocratic retention of full powers)
key_tensions: Inherited authority vs delegated authority (core kernel contest)
Divine/traditional legitimacy vs popular consent legitimacy
Stability through succession vs accountability through election
Resistance to reform (traditional authority) vs adaptive change (democratic accountability)
Zero-sum retention of monarchical power vs constitutional compromise
key_mechanisms: Constitutional compromise (power-sharing between monarch and parliament)
Divine Right invocation (theological legitimation of rule)
key_absences: Non-Western legitimacy frameworks (Confucian mandate of heaven, Islamic caliphate models)
Legitimacy crisis resolution mechanisms (what happens when inherited or delegated authority fails)
Economic base analysis (material conditions enabling monarchical vs republican forms)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The sovereign-legitimacy kernel: the shared commitment that some entity holds legitimate authority to rule over a polity
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested — monarchical reading grounds interpretive authority in tradition/theology/bloodline; republican reading grounds it in popular consent/constitutional law

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority flows downward from the sovereign through inherited right, grounded in divine sanction, tradition, and bloodline continuity
readings.authority_grounding: theological/traditional — Divine Right doctrine, age-old precedent, sanctity of dynastic succession
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiary: hereditary ruling class and aristocratic hierarchy. Victim: subjects excluded from authority participation. High ε suppression of alternative legitimacy claims. Stability through succession rules but vulnerability to succession contests. Legitimacy validation mechanism: continuity of bloodline and traditional ritual.

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority flows upward from the people through delegated consent, grounded in popular sovereignty and social contract
readings.authority_grounding: popular/contractual — consent of the governed, electoral mandate, constitutional law as expression of collective will
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiary: citizenry with voting rights and participatory mechanisms. Victim: those excluded from franchise or consent mechanisms. Moderate ε — legitimacy requires ongoing validation through elections. Accountability through removal mechanisms but vulnerability to majoritarian tyranny. Legitimacy validation mechanism: electoral cycles and constitutional adherence.

readings.commitment: Legitimate authority is dual-sourced: ceremonial/symbolic authority inherited, political authority delegated, with constitutional law mediating the boundary
readings.authority_grounding: hybrid/negotiated — constitutional settlement partitioning inherited and delegated authority spheres
readings.expected_structural_delta: Beneficiary: both hereditary monarch (retained status/income) and elected officials (policy power). Victim: those seeking pure form (absolutists and republicans both constrained). Low-to-moderate ε — compromise reduces extractiveness of both pure forms but introduces ambiguity costs. Stability through institutional separation but vulnerability to boundary disputes. Legitimacy validation mechanism: constitutional interpretation and precedent.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Monarchical axiom (authority legitimately flows from inherited divine/traditional right independent of popular will) and republican axiom (authority legitimately flows only from popular consent) cannot both be foundational in a single coherent framework. Accepting one as the ultimate source of legitimacy requires rejecting the other as the ultimate source. Constitutional hybrid does not resolve this — it partitions authority spheres rather than synthesizing the axioms.
